events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.95)
events.body:
This is a safety-type dispute filed by the driver, and the fact table contains a chat fact tagged as a threat: at 18:21 the driver wrote “Please do not smoke in the car.” [F3] and at 18:22 the rider replied “Say that again and I will punch you.” [F4], with the automated threat-keyword detection flagging “punch” in that rider message [F5]. Under SAFE-1, the appearance of threat/intimidation language in chat removes the matter from automated adjudication and requires escalation with a factual summary for human handling [F4][F5][SAFE-1]. The driver's written report repeats the same conduct at the same time point — “The passenger threatened to punch me when I asked him not to smoke” [F6] — and is consistent with, though not independent of, the chat log [F4][F6][SAFE-1].

What happened: a metered RydeTAXI trip Tampines Mall → Changi Airport T3, pickup 18:15, drop-off 18:28, charged $21.26. The ride itself was operationally normal — actual 8.8 km vs optimal 8.9 km (-0.1 km) [F1], 13.3 min vs 16 min estimate [F2] — so no route or fare issue arises and no monetary component of this incident can be computed from the fact table [F1][F2]. What is disputed: the rider's intent and severity behind the 18:22 message. The only evidence is the chat transcript and the keyword flag [F4][F5] plus the driver's own statement [F6]; there is no audio, SOS, or post-trip report metadata, and no system record of any physical act. Profile facts are recorded for both parties — rider 732-day account, 4.85 rating, 0 disputes/0 upheld in 90 days [F7]; driver 1316-day account, 4.5 rating, 427 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes/0 upheld [F8] — but profile facts cannot decide this case on their own.

Facts to check by the human reviewer: the full in-app chat transcript around 18:21–18:22 including whether any messages are missing between [F3][F4]; the keyword-flag metadata timestamp and algorithm output for rider message #2 [F5]; whether any SOS/emergency or in-trip report was logged at or after 18:22; the driver's formal report submission time and any attached evidence [F6]; and both parties' dispute histories to assess whether this is an isolated incident or a pattern [F7][F8]. Because SAFE-1 applies, no amount is awarded and no account action is taken by this ruling.

claims.assertion: The in-app chat records the rider writing at 18:22: "Say that again and I will punch you.", a threat of physical violence directed at the driver, and the system flagged the threat keyword "punch" in that message.
The threat was made in direct response to the driver's 18:21 request not to smoke in the car, so it is tied to a lawful in-vehicle conduct request and is not an ambiguous remark.
The driver's written statement repeats and reports the same conduct — a threat of assault — which is the type of abuse SAFE-1 removes from automated adjudication and routes to human review.

The rider has a clean record on paper (732-day account, 4.85 rating, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days), but profile facts cannot decide the case and do not neutralize a recorded, system-flagged threat.

The trip itself ran normally — 8.8 km actual against 8.9 km optimal (-0.1 km) in 13.3 min against a 16 min estimate — so the safety escalation rests on the chat record rather than on any route or fare irregularity.

weaknesses: The only evidence of the threat is user-submitted chat content and the driver's own statement (F4, F5, F6); no corroborating system record (e.g. audio, SOS, or post-trip report metadata) confirms the rider's tone, intent, or the physical context the driver describes.

The rider profile is entirely clean (F7: 4.85 rating, 0 disputes, 0 upheld), which the rider will use to argue the message was a heat-of-the-moment figure of speech rather than a genuine threat, and the message is text-only so the rider can argue no physical act followed.

The driver's own profile shows a 4.5 rating (F8), slightly below the rider's 4.85, which the rider may use to suggest the driver's account is less reliable; nothing in the fact table quantifies the threat, so a human reviewer may treat this as a low-severity first incident.
No traffic, fare or no-show facts exist for this case (empty returns), so no independent system record corroborates or contradicts any part of the incident beyond the chat log.

claims.assertion: The rider sent an explicit threat of violence in the in-app chat: at 18:22, one minute after the driver's request not to smoke, the rider wrote 'Say that again and I will punch you.' This is a threat of intimidation directed at the driver.
The threat is corroborated by the automated threat-keyword detection on the rider's message (keyword 'punch', rider message #2, 18:22), so it is not merely an allegation by the driver.
The driver's written statement matches the chat record in time and content ('The passenger threatened to punch me when I asked him not to smoke. I want this reported.').

The provocation context is benign and safety-motivated: the driver's only preceding message was 'Please do not smoke in the car.' at 18:21, so the rider's threat was a response to a lawful request, not to any aggression by the driver.

The ride itself was conducted properly — actual distance 8.8 km was 0.1 km shorter than the 8.9 km optimal route and the trip took 13.3 min versus a 16 min estimate — so there is no counter-allegation of driver misconduct to weigh against the threat.
Threats and intimidation are treated by Ryde as a conduct matter that is not resolved by an automated fare ruling but escalated for human handling, with the fact summary provided to the reviewer.

The driver's account history is clean (3.6 years, rating 4.5, 427 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes, 0 upheld), which supports treating this report as a genuine safety referral rather than a fee-driven complaint; the rider's profile (2.0 years, 4.85, 0 disputes in 90 days) shows no history contradicting the chat record.

weaknesses: The rider had 0 disputes in 90 days and a 4.85 rating (F7), so the other side will argue the rider has no pattern of aggressive behaviour and that this was an isolated verbal outburst.

The threat is only in the chat transcript (F4/F5); there is no GPS, timeline or fare fact recording any physical act, so the other side may characterise it as words only with no assault, and may argue F3's request was itself provocative.
The driver's rating is 4.5 (F8), which the other side may use to suggest prior friction with riders, although no disputes were recorded.
No traffic/weather facts (get_traffic_facts returned none) and no fare facts, so no monetary component of this incident can be quantified; any restitution cannot be computed from the fact table.

points.response: Conceded on the primary fact: the rider's 18:22 message "Say that again and I will punch you." is a threat of violence on the record, and I do not contest that SAFE-1 is the governing clause.

Agreed as far as it goes — the keyword flag on "punch" (F5) shows the message was auto-detected, but it establishes only that the text contained a threat keyword, not the rider's intent or severity; SAFE-1 still sends the question to a human rather than resolving it automatically.
The driver's statement (F6) is consistent with the chat log (F4), but F6 is the driver's own submission about the same message and adds no independent corroboration beyond it.

I do not contest that the driver's 18:21 message was a lawful no-smoking request (F3), but the advocate's characterisation of it as benign cuts against treating the ride as wholly incident-free equally for both parties — the context is one minute of escalation between two messages, not a sustained campaign.

Accepted: the GPS record shows no driver misconduct to weigh — 8.8 km actual versus 8.9 km optimal and 13.3 min versus a 16 min estimate (F1, F2) — and my brief's C5 already treats the trip as operationally normal.

I agree with the requested disposition — SAFE-1 excludes automatic adjudication of threat reports (F4, F5, F6) — so the practical outcome both sides ask for is the same: escalate with a factual summary for human review, not a fare ruling.

Conceded, with one correction: profile facts (F7, F8) may not decide the case under SAFE-1, and the rider's clean record — 732-day account, 4.85 rating, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days (F7) — supports treating this as an isolated verbal incident, which is precisely the mitigating context a human reviewer should weigh alongside the escalated chat record.

Conceded — the rider's advocate states the same operative fact we rely on: the 18:22 message 'Say that again and I will punch you.' is a threat of physical violence and the system flagged the keyword 'punch' (F4, F5), the exact trigger for escalation under SAFE-1. Nothing in their brief contests it.

Agreed, and it strengthens our case: the threat followed the driver's 18:21 message 'Please do not smoke in the car.' by one minute (F3, F4), so the rider's violence was a reaction to a lawful request and no provocation by the driver is alleged under SAFE-1.

Agreed — the driver's statement reports the same threat, which is exactly why SAFE-1 removes this from automated adjudication and sends it to human review; the reviewer must treat the driver as the reporting victim, not as a party under investigation.

Their concession that profile facts cannot decide the case cuts against them: the rider's clean 732-day / 4.85 / 0-dispute record (F7) is equally incapable of explaining away a recorded, keyword-flagged threat, and the driver's 4.5 rating with 427 trips and 0 disputes (F8) cannot be used to discredit the report.

Agreed — the GPS record shows a normal trip (8.8 km actual vs 8.9 km optimal, 13.3 min vs 16 min estimate, F1, F2), so the escalation rests purely on the chat record and I seek no route or fare ruling.

Their weakness that the evidence is text-only does not weaken escalation: SAFE-1 covers threats of any kind recorded in chat, without requiring audio, SOS or physical contact, and the flagged keyword (F5) plus the driver's statement (F6) both attach to the same 18:22 incident (F4).

I keep the account-history point in its limited role: the driver's 3.6-year record with 427 trips in 90 days and 0 disputes / 0 upheld (F8) supports that this is a genuine safety referral, offered only as supporting context and never as the basis of the finding, as SAFE-1 requires.
